To test holonomic generalization in Fig. 2 , we constructed a variable tracking task formally isomorphic to the permutation of world-lines. The system consists of 10 variables (memory slots), initialized with distinct values. The input sequence consists of SWAP( v i , v j v_{i},v_{j} ) operations, representing the exchange of two memory contents. This creates a combinatorial state space governed by the symmetric group S 10 S_{10} , which contains approximately 3.6 × 10 6 3.6\times 10^{6} distinct states. Fundamentally, this task separates the syntax of the operation (the swap instruction at step t t ) from the semantics (the current values held in the variables). To evaluate out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization, we enforced a strict separation of scales: models were trained on sequence lengths L ∈ [ 1 , 50 ] L\in[1,50] (the training horizon) but evaluated on lengths L ∈ [ 51 , 5000 ] L\in[51,5000] (the extrapolation horizon). Success requires the model to learn the time-invariant generative law of the permutation operator, rather than memorizing positional correlations. To formally identify the universality class of the Holonomic Network, we analyze the partition function of the hidden state dynamics in the continuum limit.
